questions.question_text: Before a South Dakota property manager performs any services, what must be in place?
questions.correct_answer: A written management agreement with the client
distractors: A verbal fee agreement confirmed by email
A copy of the owner's deed on file
SDREC approval of the management contract
questions.explanation: A property manager and client must sign a written management agreement specifying the duties and conditions of service before the manager performs any services (ARSD 20:69:14:06). Unlike an agency agreement, it may auto-renew if it allows written cancellation.

questions.question_text: A person wants to help tenants find apartments and collect a fee, but not manage properties. What SD license do they need?
distractors: Property management license
Broker associate license
No license is required for this activity
questions.explanation: A residential rental agent license covers negotiating residential rentals and collecting rents (SDCL 36-21A-12.1). The agent works under the direct supervision of a broker or property manager and may sign leases only if authorized, with the broker endorsing them.

questions.question_text: A property manager in South Dakota collects rental deposits. Where must these funds be held?
questions.correct_answer: In a properly designated trust account
distractors: In the property manager's personal account
In the property owner's bank account directly
In a separate escrow at the title company
questions.explanation: Security deposits, damage deposits, advance fees, and rents all go into a trust account at a federally insured institution (ARSD 20:69:14:11). Tenant security deposits are carried as a separate balance in the owner's ledger or a tenant ledger.

questions.question_text: Before a timeshare project can be sold to the public in South Dakota, it must be:
distractors: Approved by the local zoning board
Listed on the state MLS system
Certified by a licensed appraiser
questions.explanation: Every time-share project must be registered with the commission annually before any interest is sold or advertised (SDCL 43-15B-2, 43-15B-3). Selling in an unregistered project is a violation the commission pursues directly.

questions.question_text: An investor personally owns eight rental houses, collects the rent, and signs the leases. Does she need a property manager license?
questions.correct_answer: No, a bona fide owner managing their own property is exempt
distractors: Yes, collecting rent always requires a license
Yes, unless she owns fewer than four units
No, but only if a licensed broker signs the leases
questions.explanation: The license law does not reach a bona fide owner or lessor performing these acts for property they own, or their regular employees (SDCL 36-21A-29(1)). Managing someone else's property for compensation is what triggers the license.

questions.question_text: A property manager is setting the security deposit on a residential lease with rent of $900 per month. What is the maximum?
questions.correct_answer: One month's rent, unless special conditions justify more
distractors: Two months' rent in every case
One and a half months' rent
There is no statutory cap on a residential security deposit
questions.explanation: A lessor may not demand a residential security deposit worth more than one month's rent, however it is labeled (SDCL 43-32-6.1). The parties may agree to more only where special conditions pose a danger to maintenance of the premises.

questions.question_text: A residential tenancy ends and the tenant gives the manager a forwarding address. When must the deposit be returned or a withholding statement sent?
questions.correct_answer: Within two weeks of termination and receipt of the address
distractors: Within thirty days of termination and receipt of the address
Within ten business days after the tenant hands over keys
Immediately upon the tenant's written demand for return
questions.explanation: The lessor must return the deposit or give a written statement of the specific reason for withholding within two weeks after the tenancy ends and the tenant's mailing address is received (SDCL 43-32-24). Only amounts needed to cover rent defaults or restore the premises may be withheld.

questions.question_text: A manager misses the statutory deadline and keeps part of a deposit in bad faith. What is the exposure?
questions.correct_answer: Punitive damages up to $200 and forfeiture of any withholding
distractors: Loss of the withholding right plus treble damages to the tenant
Punitive damages up to $2,000 and forfeiture of the lease
A $500 civil penalty collected by the state's attorney
questions.explanation: A lessor who fails to comply with the return-and-statement rules forfeits all rights to withhold any portion of the deposit, and bad-faith retention adds punitive damages capped at two hundred dollars (SDCL 43-32-24).

questions.question_text: A manager wants to enter an occupied rental unit to inspect a furnace. What notice is presumed reasonable, and what must it contain?
questions.correct_answer: 24 hours' written notice stating dates, times, and purpose
distractors: 48 hours' oral or written notice given at any reasonable hour
No advance notice, so long as entry is at a reasonable hour
Seven days' written notice delivered by certified mail
questions.explanation: A landlord must give reasonable notice at reasonable times, and twenty-four hours' written notice is presumed reasonable (SDCL 43-32-32). The notice must state the date or dates of entry, a period during normal business hours, the purpose, and how the tenant may reschedule.

questions.question_text: A manager knows methamphetamines were once manufactured in unit 4 of an eight-unit building. Must that be told to a prospective tenant of unit 4?
questions.correct_answer: Yes — actual knowledge of prior meth manufacturing must be disclosed
distractors: No — the duty attaches only to sales of the property, never to leases
Yes — but only if the tenant asks about the unit's prior history
No — the lessor must disclose only if a cleanup order was issued
questions.explanation: A lessor with actual knowledge of prior methamphetamine manufacturing on the premises must disclose it to any lessee or prospective lessee (SDCL 43-32-30). In a building of two or more units, the duty reaches only the affected unit.
